RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.label: a betrothal waiting on a word
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.description: Two betrothed colonists come to ask the lord's blessing before the wedding is held.
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.caseText:
{PETITIONER_labelShort} and {OTHER_labelShort} are promised to each other and come before the court together, which the whole colony worked out some time ago. A betrothal in this hall waits on the lord: they are asking him to say out loud that the match is a good one, so the feast can be held rather than talked about for another season.
It costs him nothing but his word, and his word is the only thing they cannot get anywhere else.
How does the lord rule?

li.label: Bless it, and set the day
li.pastLabel: the match blessed and the day set

RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.label: one task too many
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.description: A colonist asks to be excused from a named job he has no heart for.
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.caseText:
{PETITIONER_labelShort} has been put to {WORK}, has no heart for it and no hand for it, and would rather the lord took it off {PETITIONER_objective}. Somebody else would have to pick it up. That is rather the point of asking a lord instead of asking a friend.
How does the lord rule?

li.label: Refuse. The {WORK} does not do itself
Tell {PETITIONER_labelShort} to sort it out with the others
li.pastLabel: sent away to sort it out

RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.label: leave to go
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.description: An unhappy colonist asks the lord for permission to leave the colony.
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.caseText:
{PETITIONER_labelShort} has been unhappy here for a long while, and has come to say so in the one place where saying it means something. {PETITIONER_pronoun} is asking leave to go. Whether the lord grants it or not, everyone in the hall now knows {PETITIONER_pronoun} wanted to.
How does the lord rule?

li.label: Refuse. Nobody walks out on the lord
Let {PETITIONER_labelShort} go, and provisioned for the road
li.pastLabel: sent off with food for the road

RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.label: an honour to be given
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.description: A colonist who has killed for the colony asks to be paid for it, in coin the colony will not see again.
RimCourt.Court.PetitionDef.caseText:
{PETITIONER_labelShort} has killed {KILLS} people for this colony and has never heard anyone say so. {PETITIONER_pronoun} is not asking to be thanked, or not only. {PETITIONER_pronoun} knows what someone is worth who does that work, and {PETITIONER_pronoun} has put a number on it: {SILVER} silver.
Coin says it in a way words cannot, and it leaves with {PETITIONER_objective}. Words cost the colony nothing, and {PETITIONER_pronoun} will take them, but {PETITIONER_pronoun} will know what {PETITIONER_pronoun} was offered instead of what {PETITIONER_pronoun} asked for.
How does the lord rule?

li.label: Pay {PETITIONER_labelShort} the {SILVER} silver he asks
li.pastLabel: paid {SILVER} silver for the blood he spilled

li.label: Honour {PETITIONER_labelShort} before the court, and nothing more
li.pastLabel: honoured before the court, and nothing more

li.label: Rule that {PETITIONER_labelShort} did no more than his duty
